newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to allow bond trading on Bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to allow bond trading on Bolsa.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Ministry has developed a scheme that would allow trading of Mexican sovereign and Brady bonds on the Mexican stock exchange (Bolsa) before the end of the month.

The players will be brokerage houses and banks, who will be allowed to obtain the securities on foreign markets and register them with the bolsa before selling them to investors, according to government officials.
The amount of outstanding paper available to be traded will be about $30.15 billion, and will be traded in dollars but liquidated in pesos, government officials said.
The new plan was presented to the Mexican Banker's Association at a meeting on Wednesday by Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz.
At a press conference, Antonio Del Valle, president of the banker's association said the scheme would give Mexican banks another instrument to offer investors.

"Brady bonds, all of the UMS global bonds, the 30-year, the 20 year and the five years from the end of the month will be able to be traded in the Mexican Stock market, and will be able to be obtained by investors...," he said.
The plan was approved in a recent session of a special committee of the bolsa.
The amount of bonds that can be traded is expected to be limited to seven at the start and then to be gradually increased.
According to a discussion paper sent to Mexican brokerage houses the following bond issues will be traded at first:
- UMS FRN, due 2001
- UMS Par, due 2016
- UMS Discount, due 2019
A wide variety of peso-denominated paper already trades through the trading floor at the Mexican stock exchange, including Cetes or treasury bills, and development bonds or Bondes.
Analysts said the plan may be aimed at providing liquidity for the new private pension funds, the Afores, and would likely not affect market prices for the outstanding paper.
They said they did not think it would be a big deal for either the Brady or Eurobond markets.
"I don't think that it will necessarily be a big event to watch. It is not a factor that will affect market prices," ING Barings Latin America Debt Strategist, Raul Elizalde, said.
According to the Emerging Markets Traders Assocation, total trading volume for Mexican Bradies in 1996 was $353.04 billion.
For the Mexican sovereigns, the total trading volume was $111.86 billion in 1996, the association said.
The private pension funds will begin operation on July 1 this year. They are seen providing a new market for peso-linked debt.
((-- Mexico City newsroom (525) 728 9559))
